q-340768.name: Question 1
q-340768.problem:
$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx) \\ g(x) & ∼\frac{{c}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{c}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)+{d}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)\end{aligned}
$$

Let $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ be $2\pi $-periodic extensions of some functions from $x\in [-\pi ,\pi )$ to $x\in R$ with the Fourier series shown above. What is the $6\text{th}$ Fourier sine coefficient of $-3f(x)-2g(x)?$
q-340768.worked_solution:
Let $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ be $2\pi $-periodic functions with Fourier series

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }({a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)), \\ g(x) & ∼\frac{{c}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }({c}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)+{d}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)).\end{aligned}
$$

Then for any constants $\alpha $ and $\beta $,

$$
\alpha f(x)+\beta g(x)∼\frac{\alpha {a}_{0}+\beta {c}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }((\alpha {a}_{n}+\beta {c}_{n})\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)+(\alpha {b}_{n}+\beta {d}_{n})\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)).
$$

Using the linearity property of Fourier series, the corresponding Fourier coefficients of $-3f(x)-2g(x)$ are

- $-3{a}_{0}-2{c}_{0}$ for the constant coefficient,

- $-3{a}_{n}-2{c}_{n},$ $n\ge 1$ for the cosine coefficients, and

- $-3{b}_{n}-2{d}_{n},$ $n\ge 1$ for the sine coefficients.

Therefore, the $6$th sine coefficient of $-3f(x)-2g(x)$ is

$$
-3{b}_{6}-2{d}_{6}.
$$

Let $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ be $2\pi $-periodic functions with Fourier series

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & ∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }({a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)), \\ g(x) & ∼\frac{{c}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }({c}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)+{d}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)).\end{aligned}
$$

Then for any constants $\alpha $ and $\beta $,

$$
\alpha f(x)+\beta g(x)∼\frac{\alpha {a}_{0}+\beta {c}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }((\alpha {a}_{n}+\beta {c}_{n})\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)+(\alpha {b}_{n}+\beta {d}_{n})\operatorname{sin}⁡(nx)).
$$

Using the linearity property of Fourier series, the corresponding Fourier coefficients of $4f(x)-g(x)$ are

- $4{a}_{0}-{c}_{0}$ for the constant coefficient,

- $4{a}_{n}-{c}_{n},$ $n\ge 1$ for the cosine coefficients, and

- $4{b}_{n}-{d}_{n},$ $n\ge 1$ for the sine coefficients.

Therefore, the $5$th sine coefficient of $4f(x)-g(x)$ is

$$
4{b}_{5}-{d}_{5}.
$$

To determine whether $f$ is even or odd, we compare $f(-x)$ and $f(x):$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-x) & =(-x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(-x) \\  & =-x\operatorname{cos}⁡(x) \\  & =-f(x).\end{aligned}
$$

Since $f(-x)=-f(x),$ we have that $f$ is odd.

For Fourier series on $[-\pi ,\pi ],$ the cosine coefficients are given by

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }f(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)\,\text{d}x,
$$

and the constant coefficient is

$$
{a}_{0}=\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Here, $f(x)$ is odd and $\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)$ is even, so $f(x)\operatorname{cos}⁡(nx)$ is odd. Also, $f(x)$ itself is odd.

Now, the integral of an odd function over $[-\pi ,\pi ]$ is $0.$ Thus, ${a}_{n}=0$ for all $n\ge 1,$ and ${a}_{0}=0.$

Therefore, the function $f(x)$ is $\text{odd}$ and the $\text{cosine terms}$ in its Fourier series must be zero.
